clue.text: For clarification, a big gun admits I was wrong

definitions.note: a phrase of purpose, read as 'clarifying', the participle the answer gives

indicators.note: something that was wrong is out of order, so the letters of these clue words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A senior figure, asked to clear things up, confesses a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admits' looks like the joining verb but is part of the fodder: A BIG GUN, ADMITS and I make fourteen letters, which 'was wrong' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Removing ambiguity from something is a way of clarifying its meaning.

clue.text: What you might get eating duck in the doldrums?

definitions.text: What you might get eating duck
definitions.meaning: a duck is covered in fine soft feathers, which could end up between your lips as you eat it
an idiom for being low-spirited or gloomy

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about what happens when you eat duck and feel listless.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is literal: the soft feathers of a duck would be in your mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a dejected, miserable expression, the mood of someone stuck in a slump.

clue.text: Small schoolchildren brought up mistakes

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing something up reads it from bottom to top, so these letters run backwards

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
schoolchildren are pupils

explanation.surface: Young pupils raised badly, or making errors.
explanation.definitionFit: Slip-ups are minor errors or blunders, so they are mistakes.

clue.text: Old couple spot leading writer

indicators.note: one piece leading another goes in front of it, so this word comes first

parts.note: a spot or stain is a mark
twain is an archaic word for two, a pair

explanation.surface: An elderly pair recognise a top author.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark Twain, author of Huckleberry Finn, is a famous American writer.

clue.text: Skinhead infiltrates stylish marriage as one

parts.note: in means fashionable or stylish

indicators.note: something that infiltrates gets inside another thing, so this letter is put within the others

parts.note: a marriage is a union
the head of the word skin is its first letter

explanation.surface: A shaven-headed thug sneaks into a fashionable wedding, all together.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing things in unison means acting together, simultaneously, as one body.

clue.text: Model is nude without them?

indicators.note: to model is to shape or form anew, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A life model is naked because she has no underwear on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' first looks like the person posing, but it is the anagram signal; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Undies is informal for underwear, so a model without underclothes would indeed be nude.

clue.text: Group of climatologists picked up language

indicators.note: in a down clue, picking letters up lifts them so they read upwards, from the bottom
a group of letters is taken from inside the word that follows

explanation.surface: A set of climate scientists learnt a new tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Tamil is a Dravidian tongue spoken in southern India and Sri Lanka.

clue.text: New firms occupy 11, a divided city

indicators.note: firms that occupy something sit inside it, so these letters go within the other pair

parts.note: the figure 11 is two ones side by side, each read as the letter I
COS is short for companies, which are firms

explanation.surface: Fresh businesses move into a split city, with 11 referring to another clue.
explanation.walkthrough: '11' looks like a cross-reference to the clue for 11 across but is read as two digits, each a 1, each the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicosia, capital of Cyprus, has been split by a buffer zone since 1974.

clue.text: What someone should say to orotund guy barking in corner?

indicators.note: one piece in another sits inside it, so the shuffled letters go within the other word

parts.note: to be in a corner is to be in a hole, a tight spot

indicators.note: barking is slang for mad, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Advice for silencing a pompous man ranting in a corner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barking' reads as the man's ranting but is the anagram signal; 'in a corner' is the idiom 'in a hole', which holds the scrambled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is a command to be quiet, the thing one would say to shut up a windbag.

clue.text: Which church wants money to retain rare collection?

indicators.note: to want here is to lack, so the church letters are missing from the word
money that retains a letter holds it inside

parts.note: a pound is money, the British currency unit

explanation.surface: A query about which church needs funds to keep an unusual set of items.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Which church wants' reads as a question but means WHICH lacking CH.
explanation.definitionFit: A whip-round is an informal collection of money among a group, say for a colleague's leaving gift.

clue.text: Chairman welcomes accountant in former colony

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so these letters go inside

parts.note: Chairman Mao led Communist China
CA is a chartered accountant

explanation.surface: A party leader greets a bookkeeper in an old overseas territory.
explanation.definitionFit: Macao was a Portuguese colony until it passed back to China in 1999.

clue.text: One lot of teachers tackles international language

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: to tackle something is to take it on and grip it, so this letter goes inside

parts.note: the NUT was the National Union of Teachers in Britain

explanation.surface: A teachers' union takes on a global tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Inuit is used for the tongue of the Arctic peoples of Canada and Greenland, also called Inuktitut.

clue.text: Papers noticed missing head placed on pedestal

parts.note: identity papers are ID

indicators.note: without its head, the word loses its first letter

parts.note: to realise something is to notice it

explanation.surface: Documents spotted without a bust being set on a plinth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing head' takes the R from REALISED, leaving EALISED.
explanation.definitionFit: To idealise someone is to regard them as perfect, figuratively putting them on a pedestal.

clue.text: He's willing to start novel about Spain

indicators.note: one piece about another surrounds it
novel means new, so these letters take a new order

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: A writer keen to begin a book about Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' passes for a book but signals rearranging TO START, which goes round E.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who makes a will leaving their estate is said to be willing it, a pun on the legal role.

clue.text: Old capital mostly backed language

indicators.note: backed means sent back, so the letters read in reverse
mostly means all but the last letter is kept

parts.note: Havana is the capital of Cuba

explanation.surface: An ancient city, largely reversed, gives a tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Navaho, also spelt Navajo, is a Native American tongue of the south-western United States.

clue.text: Language articles in Frankish damned hard going

indicators.note: the articles sit in the other letters, inside them
damned suggests something wrecked, so these letters are rearranged
hard going means the letter for hard goes away

parts.note: H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard
A is the indefinite article, here twice

explanation.surface: A grammar note: Frankish articles are tough to master.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hard going' looks like a comment on difficulty but removes the letter for hard before 'damned' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Afrikaans is a tongue of South Africa that grew out of Dutch.

clue.text: Hate terrifying rise in river

indicators.note: the shuffled letters are put in, within the river's name

parts.note: the Avon is an English river

indicators.note: something terrifying throws things into disorder, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A scary rise in the level of a river.
explanation.definitionFit: An aversion is a strong dislike, close to loathing.

clue.text: President ignoring Romney's mission

indicators.note: ignoring a part means leaving it out of the name

parts.note: François Mitterrand was President of France
Mitt Romney is the American politician

explanation.surface: A leader snubs a rival politician's diplomatic task.
explanation.walkthrough: The President is French, not American: drop Mitt Romney's first name from Mitterrand.
explanation.definitionFit: An errand is a short trip to do a task, a small mission.

clue.text: He contradicts judge's true version

parts.note: a referee, ref, is a judge of play

indicators.note: a version of a word is a different form of it, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An umpire gives his honest account.
explanation.definitionFit: One who refutes argues that a claim is false, so he contradicts it.

clue.text: Catch fast runner in part of cricket match

indicators.note: the bird goes in the cricket term, inside it

parts.note: an over is a set of six balls bowled in cricket
the rhea is a large flightless South American bird that runs fast

explanation.surface: A cricket catch taken by a speedy player during an over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catch' looks like cricket but means to hear by chance.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch a remark is to hear it, and to overhear is to catch words not meant for you.

clue.text: Heather hides books such as Fifty Shades of Grey

definitions.text: such as Fifty Shades of Grey

indicators.note: to hide something is to keep it inside, so these letters go within

parts.note: erica is the botanical name for heather
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: A woman named Heather conceals her steamy novels.
explanation.definitionFit: Fifty Shades of Grey is a famous example of sexually explicit fiction.

clue.text: Language style adopted in rising

indicators.note: something adopted is taken in, so these letters go inside

parts.note: dash is flair or style

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising reads letters upwards, from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A tongue's style taken up during an uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: Danish is the tongue of Denmark.

clue.text: Finished broadcasting for a thief undergoing rehab

indicators.note: a thief undergoing rehab is being reformed, so the letters are reformed into a new order

explanation.surface: A criminal in rehabilitation has stopped transmitting.
explanation.definitionFit: A station or programme that has stopped transmission is no longer on air.

clue.text: Heroic Anglo-Saxon author satirised clothes

indicators.note: to clothe something is to cover it, so the answer is wrapped within these words

explanation.surface: A writer pokes fun at the dress of an old English hero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' looks like a noun but is a verb: the words clothe the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Horsa, with his brother Hengist, is a legendary leader of the first Anglo-Saxon settlers in Britain.

clue.text: Eastern city took off with inflow of local currency

indicators.note: an inflow brings the letter into the others
off means awry, so these letters go wrong

parts.note: Y stands for the yen, currency of Japan, the city's own

explanation.surface: A city's cash streams in after someone takes off.
explanation.definitionFit: Kyoto is a historic Japanese city, once the imperial capital.

clue.text: A brief word of thanks in Turkey's Turkic language

indicators.note: these letters go in the code for Turkey

parts.note: TR is the international code for Turkey
ta is a short British way of saying thanks

explanation.surface: A quick thank-you in a Turkish tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Tatar is a Turkic tongue spoken in Tatarstan in Russia.

clue.text: Current coupling involves sex for reproduction

definitions.note: read as 'reproducing', the participle the answer gives

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current

indicators.note: to involve something is to enfold it, so these letters go inside

parts.note: mating is coupling
it is slang for sex

explanation.surface: A modern pairing that is about sex to have children.
explanation.definitionFit: Copying something is reproducing it, so mimicking a thing makes a reproduction.

clue.text: Respite pair enjoys each night abroad without children

indicators.note: to enjoy something is to have it, hold it within

parts.note: a brace is a pair, as of game birds

indicators.note: abroad means scattered widely, so these letters are spread into a new order

parts.note: SP stands for sine prole, Latin for without issue, used in genealogy

explanation.surface: A childless couple enjoy a night away from home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without children' is the genealogists' s.p. (sine prole), not a hint to drop letters; 'abroad' rearranges the night.
explanation.definitionFit: A breathing space is a short rest or pause, a respite.
